requiredScope: The complete required language and role scope remains in force.
binding: Process declarations in supplied order. An explicit complete catalog settles whether the preceding temporary schema has a relation named text at each definition. If no such relation is declared, the default path resolves the unqualified type to pg_catalog.text. A relation's declared type stays bound after subsequent declarations. The explicitly qualified pg_catalog.text always uses that builtin. An open catalog leaves a possible earlier object unresolved. A declared earlier temporary text relation makes the unqualified type a composite, outside the scalar text form.
externalInterpretation: Use the same ordered declarations, native default data-type search path, temporary session state and physical table. Record the exact native type identity at the three fixture tables independently of IR.
observations: A previously declared unqualified text field has the builtin OID 25 after later introduction of the same name.
An explicitly qualified text field has OID 25 while the earlier temporary composite type is visible.
The same unqualified type name used after creation of a temporary relation called text denotes its composite row type.
A complete value that reads a builtin text field retains its physical reference, native type, label, NULL and exact text bytes.

finite.completeness: Recover table, occurrence count, physical slot and ONLY policy from independently observed public values.

exploration.requiredForms: Vary repeated projections, field order, quoted labels and inherited scan policy across both physically distinct text tables.

analysis: Resolve an unqualified text declaration in a complete catalog before introducing any temporary shadow.
Preserve the same builtin slot when the temporary shadow is introduced after the declaration.
Resolve explicitly qualified pg_catalog.text after that shadow has been introduced.
negative: Reject an unqualified declaration in a partial catalog when a temporary shadow cannot be ruled out.
Reject a text projection using the composite row type that was declared before the ordinary table.
faults: Discard complete declaration knowledge during construction of an explicitly complete context.
Ignore a visible earlier temporary composite when resolving an unqualified type.

evidence.P01: Record both the selected slot and the native type chosen under the actual declaration order.
evidence.P02: Resolve complete declarations and reject the unresolved and incompatible kinds.
evidence.P03: Use catalog knowledge only while binding; retain the resolved role and coordinates.
evidence.P04: Compose table headings and type positions with existing projection roles.
evidence.P05: Use the established immutable field and occurrence values.
evidence.P06: Compare exact typed rows for both published and original SQL.
evidence.Q01: Audit complete versus partial catalog propagation and temporary shadow recognition.
evidence.Q02: Check all direct finite identities and specified positive analyzed inputs.
evidence.Q03: Compare declaration ordering and both unqualified and qualified type lookup against native server type identities.
evidence.Q04: Compare SQL through both pinned PostgreSQL releases with native data and deterministic labels.
evidence.Q05: Bind the selected verifier, runtime declarations and exact staged distribution to the evidence.

trust: The caller's declarations faithfully describe their matching catalog state.
The PostgreSQL type OID behavior of the pinned releases.
The independently observed native SQL rows and construction path.
